canonical_touch_input_laws: Finger first: every primary action works by direct tap or native scroll without hover.
Use Pointer Events so touch, mouse and pen share one interaction path.
Physical press feedback begins on pointerdown rather than waiting for click.
Effective targets are approximately 44x44 CSS px or larger even when visuals are smaller.
Direct manipulation beats edge hunting; desktop pointer behavior preserves the same mental model as touch.
Native touch scroll owns touch physics; do not recreate iPad momentum in JavaScript.
A mouse drag adapter uses a threshold so a tap remains activation and a drag becomes pan without also activating the item.
Horizontal/vertical rails declare the correct touch-action axis; ordinary controls use manipulation.
Hover may enhance but never own information, affordance or action.
Adapt by layout/orientation/pointer capabilities rather than UA device branching.
Pointer capture is bounded and released on up/cancel/blur/loss-of-capture/teardown.
One gesture has one result; scroll-drag cannot also trigger click/enter.
No custom mouse inertia by default.
Reduced motion must preserve state and interaction feedback.

high_confidence_cross_supported: Depth indicates manipulability, not hierarchy or generic surface importance.
Non-manipulable page/content/shell surfaces remain flat by default.
Manipulable controls may use a dark external ledge/drop plus a subtle internal light to communicate physical affordance.
Pressed state physically collapses toward the base plane.
Inset treatment is reserved for an actual receiving/adjusting field, not decoration.
Strict bicolor material uses only its two theme colors across surface/text/border/depth and does not synthesize decorative helper tones.
reconstructed_v9_observations_not_global: The reconstructed specimen visually reinforces relief only on manipulable controls and flat non-action areas.
It uses external dark shadow plus internal highlight and a collapsing pressed state.
It also uses bg/surface/ink/accent/shadow/light roles and a free accent-color wheel, so its literal palette implementation is not compatible with the strict two-color shared owner.

sound_evidence.durable_conclusion: These names prove selector experimentation with selectable response sounds, but the R05 authority sources inspected do not establish them as a canonical sound owner, Current set or Human Accepted set.
sound_evidence.safe_continuation: Keep sound profiles local/candidate until a durable sound owner or explicit acceptance evidence is identified; any eventual shared sound owner should be orthogonal to the canonical pointer/gesture contract.

negative_knowledge.rule: Never use version number as authority across lineages.

negative_knowledge.rule: Never equate controls-v9 reconstructed evidence with Human Accepted physical material.
Never promote touch-first v2 because it is newer.
negative_knowledge.reason: Its manifest explicitly requires browser evidence plus Human acceptance; v1 remains Current in the canonical SPEC.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not raise content, cards, windows or shells merely to create visual richness.
negative_knowledge.reason: Material v2 corrects the law to depth=manipulability.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not use decorative third colors or color-mix helper tones in the strict bicolor material owner.
negative_knowledge.reason: Bicolor manifest and Design Kernel candidate both constrain extra colors to non-decorative semantics.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not transplant the reconstructed V9 free accent wheel into material.bicolor.
negative_knowledge.reason: It would violate exactly-two-theme-colors and no-helper-tones constraints.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not promote selector V45's theme or sound lists to shared canon from lab evidence alone.
negative_knowledge.reason: No R05 authority source establishes Current/Human Accepted sound or theme ownership for those lists.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not require hover, tiny precision, a hidden scrollbar, right click, double click or modifiers for essential action.
negative_knowledge.reason: Canonical touch-first contract forbids those dependencies.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not recreate touch momentum or globally hijack wheel events.
negative_knowledge.reason: Native touch physics remains owner; wheel-to-axis translation is opt-in and rail-scoped.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not allow a pointer drag/scroll to activate the same row/control.
negative_knowledge.reason: Touch-first one-gesture-one-result and Study negative target independently reject this failure.

negative_knowledge.rule: Do not refactor product-specific skins just because tactile laws are shared.
negative_knowledge.reason: Shared laws/primitives do not imply a shared skin; ownership must remain capability-specific.

Preserved twelve negative-knowledge rules that prevent known visual, gesture and authority regressions.
